Use the two supplied images ONLY as style references for their vivid ultramarine and ivory duotone, finely grained print texture, sharp classical stone architecture, monumental scale, and quiet metaphysical atmosphere. Scene: two parallel monumental stone aqueduct-like pedestrian bridges cross one deep, dry desert canyon between the same two chalk-white plateaus. Both bridges are intact, span the same distance, and have continuous level stone decks. The nearer bridge is supported by three broad elegant semicircular arches; the farther bridge has a rhythm of many narrower semicircular arches. Their different structures should be immediately legible while their common crossing is clear. Show them in one coherent oblique architectural view, separated by a generous visible strip of canyon, each running from the left foreground plateau toward the right middle-distance plateau. The arches open onto deep ultramarine shadow. Bridges must have plausible masonry and clean, simple, unornamented classical proportions, with low stone parapets. A single very small solitary human silhouette on the nearer bridge establishes enormous scale. Empty dry mountains on the horizon, spacious open sky, long sharply defined afternoon shadows, no water, vegetation, city, vehicles, broken architecture, floating structures, electronics, or futuristic elements.

Composition: restrained, legible, one unified landscape, not a diptych. Keep both bridges and the main architectural subject within the central 75 percent of the image, with calm sky above and dark canyon below. A strong rhythmic contrast between the two sets of arches, enough negative space, precise perspective, convincing geometry. No extra intersecting bridges or maze.

Color and finish: entirely saturated ULTRAMARINE BLUE and pale ivory duotone. Deepest shadows approximately #08004D, core blue #1600B8, middle blue #4B40D1, pale highlights #F3F2F2. Vivid Yves-Klein-like ultramarine, chalk-white sunlit stone, crisp high contrast. Absolutely no teal, cyan, slate, denim, gray-blue, powder-blue, sepia, or natural stone beige. Extremely fine visible stochastic stipple grain throughout, like a high-quality risograph print or dithered architectural render, with detailed stone surfaces.
